title: Atoms
subject: Chemistry

English.simple_explanation: Atoms are tiny building blocks that make up matter such as air, water, rocks, and our bodies.
English.detailed_explanation: An atom has a central nucleus containing protons and neutrons, with electrons found around the nucleus. The number of protons identifies the element.
English.everyday_example: A glass of water is made of many tiny water molecules, and those molecules are made from atoms.

common_misconceptions: Atoms are extremely small, but they are not simply tiny solid balls.
think_question: If atoms are so small, how can many atoms together make a solid object?

reasoning_guide.correct_feedback: Good reasoning: you explained that many tiny atoms together make larger materials.
reasoning_guide.partial_feedback: Connect the small size of one atom to the huge number of atoms in an object.
reasoning_guide.misconception_feedback: Atoms are real parts of matter. Focus on how a very large number of them combine to make an object.

challenge.question: Name the three common subatomic particles introduced in a basic atom model.
challenge.hint: One is positive, one is neutral, and one is negative.
progressive_hints: One is positive, one is neutral, and one is negative.
The positive and neutral particles are in the nucleus; the negative particle is an electron.
Name the positive particle first, then the neutral one, then the negative one.
challenge.solution: The particles are protons, neutrons, and electrons.

quiz_questions.question: Which particle in an atom has a positive charge?
quiz_questions.explanation: Protons have a positive electric charge.
quiz_questions.hint: The negatively charged particle is the electron.
progressive_hints: The negatively charged particle is the electron.
The neutral particle is the neutron, so choose the remaining positively charged particle.
